subject: Clearline Financial - private deployment discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@clearline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: private deployment options for Clearline - actions

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from my side so we have shared expectations and next steps. Please correct me where I've missed anything.

Summary of primary pain points you shared:
- Regulated payments workload: PHI/PFI scope and strict retention policies; auditability is mandatory.
- No cloud-managed secrets allowed for production crypto keys; must use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) with key custody control.
- Network isolation: production inference must not egress to public internet; restricted outbound ports and allow-listing only.
- Maintenance window constraints: planned monthly maintenance with strict rollback commitments.

Current stack and constraints you described:
- Core stack: on-prem Kubernetes (K8s 1.25) running in Clearline DC with Palo Alto firewall and a private transit to their co-lo.
- Secrets: Thales HSM for signing and key storage; currently used via PKCS#11.
- CI/CD: GitLab self-hosted; artifacts hosted on internal Nexus repo.
- Ops: No external agents running on the control plane; everything must be auditable and approvable by security.

Success criteria you called out (what a successful pilot looks like):
1) Private control plane inside Clearline VPC/Network with zero-public-egress from model inference nodes.
2) Plug-in for customer-managed KMS/HSM (PKCS#11) so keys never leave customer boundary.
3) Audit logs and token-level tracing stored in your SIEM (ability to forward logs to Splunk in near-real time).
4) Sizing: baseline throughput of ~250 concurrent requests peak with 100ms p95 target for 512-token sequences (pilot scope).

Risks / open questions we need to validate:
- Whether the Thales HSM exposes the APIs we need for KMS integration (we'll validate PKCS#11 endpoints).
- Network routing for model updates: can on-site ops accept signed model tarballs via an internal SFTP/air-gap transfer?
- Backup/DR expectations for model artifacts and KV cache state.

Proposed next steps (action owners & timelines):
1) Aisha/Redwood: send a short technical checklist for the KMS/HSM endpoints and firewall egress requirements. (ACTION: Aisha — by Mon 2026-05-25)
2) Dev/Redwood infra lead: schedule a 60-minute tech deep-dive with Clearline infra/security to review PKCS#11, network ports, and model distribution options. (ACTION: Dev — propose slots)
3) Clearline: share a sanitized network diagram and any proxy/egress rules we should know about. (ACTION: Marta — upload by 2026-05-27)
4) Mutual: NDA + data handling addendum for pilot; attach initial NDA here for signature.

Attachments: clearline-network-requirements.xlsx (worksheet we'll use to collect answers), network-topology-draft.pdf (placeholder we can annotate).

I copied Marissa from our Solutions team so she can help with the compliance checklist and DOCS package. If that plan looks right, I'll schedule the tech deep-dive this week.

Thanks —

Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@clearline.com>

Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: private deployment options for Clearline - actions

Hi Aisha —

This matches our discussion, thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from security:

- KMS / HSM: We must keep keys in the Thales HSM. Any Redwood component that needs to sign or decrypt must call into our HSM. We cannot export private keys.
- Air-gap/model updates: For the pilot we prefer transferring model bundles via an internal SFTP appliance. No automatic pull from external registries.
- Network: We can open a strict set of outbound IPs/ports to Redwood management nodes for orchestration if needed, but only over mutual TLS and after a security review.

I'll upload our sanitized network diagram and the contact for our infra/security folks by EOD Wednesday (2026-05-27). We also need to see a brief runbook of how you handle rollback/patching for private deployments.

One more ask: can you confirm whether Redwood supports PKCS#11 and whether you have a documented integration with Thales or Lunasa-style HSMs?

Thanks —
Marta
Head of Cloud Security | Clearline Financial
Marta.Lopez@clearline.com
[Inline: signature with phone]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@clearline.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: private deployment options for Clearline - technical notes

Hi Marta / Aisha —

Thanks for the details. A few technical clarifications from our infra team (high level):

1) PKCS#11 / HSM: Redwood Private supports integration with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 and/or the KMIP protocol. We can call into an on-prem HSM from the inference nodes so private keys never leave your boundary.

2) Model updates / air-gap: We support both pull and push workflows. For your requirement we can support an SFTP-based signed model bundle ingestion workflow: ops places signed tarball in the SFTP, our agent (running in your network) validates signature (using public key you provide), verifies checksum, and loads the model into the runtime. No outbound pulls required.

3) Network / egress: For the private control plane there are two common patterns we recommend:
   - Fully isolated control plane: no outbound egress from model nodes. Control plane runs behind your firewall; model artifacts are staged via internal transfer.
   - Peered minimal control plane: small set of management endpoints in our managed region with mutual TLS; traffic limited to orchestration and telemetry (you control allow-list).

4) KMS UX: We can support PKCS#11 calls directly from the runtime and/or integrate with an internal KMS proxy your ops team runs. We will not persist any private key material.

5) Observability/audit: We can forward structured audit logs (token-level metadata, not PII content) to your Splunk instance via an internal syslog/HTTPS endpoint. We will add log redaction controls in pilot config.

Next technical step: proposer slots for a focused session (60–90 min) with your infra + security + ops to validate PKCS#11 endpoints, firewall rules, and the SFTP workflow. I can run a short demo of the signed-bundle process.

Proposed times: Tue 2026-05-26 09:00–10:30 PT or Wed 2026-05-27 14:00–15:30 PT. Let me know which works and we'll send calendar invites with an agenda.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
